parts.label: Part 1
parts.article:
Part one.

You will hear a telephone conversation between a young man who wants to get a summer job in the USA and an agent.

First, you have some time to look at questions one to five.

Now listen carefully and answer questions one to five.

Hi, USA Summer Camps, Nicola speaking. How can I help you?

Um, I want to get a job in the USA this summer, and I saw an advert on your website, and it said I should call this number if I wanted more information.

Right. So you're interested in working in a summer camp?

That's working with children, is it?

Yes. Lots of children go away to summer camp in the USA, and the jobs we're advertising are for what are called counselors. That means you're with the children the whole day, twenty-four hours.

Right.

So what would I be doing exactly?

Everything. You'd be working with them, playing with them, teaching them, everything.

Your ad said there were different sorts of positions, general and specialists.

Yes. For the general counselors, they're asking for people who have experience of working with children, but it has to be as a leader of some sort.

Hmm. I'm not sure. What I'm really interested in is sport.

You might be more interested in being a specialist counselor then. They focus on one particular area. It doesn't have to be a sport, but mostly it is.

Would tennis be okay for that?

Absolutely. You might find yourself coaching other sports as well, though. They do a big range usually. That's what most of the kids are interested in, and of course, a lot of it's outdoor stuff.

So they wouldn't be so interested in something like art?

Oh, yes, they would be. Anything you're enthusiastic about and can help younger kids with.

Okay. Well, I'd be really interested in working with kids in both those areas. Now, about times, uh, the ad said the job was for twelve weeks?

Eight, actually, but most people stay on in the US for another three or four weeks and go traveling.

Yeah, I'd really like to do that. There are lots of places I'd like to see in America. So when would I need to be there?

June. Then you carry on to August and do your traveling after that, so you're back home in September.

That's perfect. Well, that all sounds great. But about the job, do I just pick it up as I go along?

No, you get there a week before the kids arrive, and that time's spent on training, so you'll learn all about the camp and working with American children and dealing with homesickness, all that kind of thing.

Right.

Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions six to ten.

Now listen and answer questions six to ten.

And I presume I'd be okay as far as my age goes. I'll be nineteen by then.

That's the minimum age officially, though they do occasionally accept people of eighteen if they have special skills that are in demand.

And how much would I actually get paid?

You get a total of nine hundred and eighty-five US dollars. You get a couple of hundred dollars more if you're over twenty-one. But that won't apply to you, so you should end up with quite a bit of money to go traveling with when you're finished.

Great. There's tons I want to see, New York, San Francisco, the Grand Canyon.

But you do have to pay for your own insurance before you start out. That costs a hundred and thirty-eight pounds sterling.

That's in case I get ill or anything?

Yes, or you lose your luggage or have to cancel.

Right. And there was something in the ad about a check of some kind because I'd be working with children?

Yes, that's right. I forgot to mention that, and it's very important. You have to be checked by the police here in the UK, and that costs thirty-six pounds.

That's okay. Is there anything else I should know as far as money goes?

Well, just that if you register with us to work on the summer camp, you can go on a Discover America tour afterwards. A lot of camp counselors do that, and we can offer you a discount on that. And of course, you're bound to make lots of friends, so you'll have people to travel with.

Right. Well, I'm definitely interested in the whole thing. So what should I do next?

Well, I'll give you our website address, and you can fill in the application form. You can fill it in online or...

That is the end of part one. You now have one minute to check your answers to part one.

analyses.content: 录音中明确提到做普通辅导员需要有与孩子共事的经验，并且必须具备某种“leader（领导者）”的经历。
你可能听到“experience of working with children”就急于寻找后面的词，要注意听转折词“but”后面跟出的核心要求。

Your ad said there were different sorts of positions, general and specialists. Yes. For the general counselors, they're asking for people who have experience of working with children, but it has to be as a leader of some sort.
录音中男生主动询问“tennis（网球）”这项运动是否可以作为专业辅导员的技能，女生给出了肯定的回答“Absolutely”。
答案是由提问的男生说出的，你可能会忽略提问者的发言而只关注回答者，一定要注意听双方互动确认的信息。
You might be more interested in being a specialist counselor then. They focus on one particular area. It doesn't have to be a sport, but mostly it is. Would tennis be okay for that? Absolutely.
男生询问工作是否是十二周，女生纠正说实际上是“eight（八）”周，随后才去旅行。
你可能会听到提问中的“twelve”或者后面的“three or four”就直接写上，要注意听女生的纠正和具体对应“工作”的时间。
Now, about times, uh, the ad said the job was for twelve weeks? Eight, actually. But most people stay on in the US for another three or four weeks and go traveling.
男生问什么时候需要到达那里，女生明确回答是“June（六月）”开始。
录音中紧接着提到了“August”和“September”，你需要根据问题区分清楚起点的月份和后续旅行结束的时间。
So when would I need to be there? June. Then you carry on to August and do your traveling after that, so you're back home in September.
录音中提到你需要在孩子到达前一周去营地，这段时间专门用来做“training（培训）”。
题目中的“first week”被替换成了录音里的“a week before”，你可能没跟上替换节奏，要注意抓住紧跟其后的核心动作词。

Well, that all sounds great, but about the job, do I just pick it up as I go along? No. You get there a week before the kids arrive, and that time's spent on training, so you'll learn all about the camp and working with American children and dealing with homesickness, all that kind of thing.
男生说自己到时就“nineteen（十九）”岁了，女生确认这正是官方规定的最低年龄。
录音里提到了干扰项“eighteen”，但那是针对有特殊技能的特例，并不是题目所问的官方普适年龄。

And I presume I'd be okay as far as my age goes. I'll be nineteen by then. That's the minimum age officially, though they do occasionally accept people of eighteen if they have special skills that are in demand.
女生直接回答总共可以拿到“985”美元的薪水。
你可能会听到后面的“a couple of hundred”或“twenty-one”而产生混淆，要注意这些是满21岁的附加条件，并不是基础薪资。
And how much would I actually get paid? You get a total of nine hundred and eighty-five US dollars. You get a couple of hundred dollars more if you're over twenty-one,
录音中明确指出在出发前你必须为自己的“insurance（保险）”买单，花费为138英镑。
你可能会先关注到后文的138英镑价格而错过前面的核心名词，要注意提前预判填空处需要的是一个物品或服务。
But you do have to pay for your own insurance before you start out. That costs a hundred and thirty-eight pounds sterling.
女生强调必须要在英国本地接受“police（警察）”的背景审查，并且花费刚好是36英镑。
题目要填的是check的前置定语，你可能会只听到被动语态的“checked by”而没有迅速抓取到动作的发起者。

And there was something in the ad about a check of some kind because I'd be working with children? Yes, that's right. I forgot to mention that, and it's very important. You have to be checked by the police here in the UK, and that costs thirty-six pounds.
录音指出很多辅导员夏令营结束后会参加美国探索之旅，并且可以提供“discount（折扣）”给你。
题目中的“on travel in America”对应了录音里的“Discover America tour”，你要能快速识别出这个词汇替换并抓取后面的宾语。
Well, just that if you register with us to work on the summer camp, you can go on a Discover America tour afterwards. A lot of camp counselors do that, and we can offer you a discount on that.
